summary.intent: Run the full autonomous post-execute-phase pipeline for GSD phase 66 (API schema cutover, IPNS publish gate, tombstone) — covering verify, secure, validate, simplify, SDK E2E gate, CodeRabbit review, ship, and resolve PR reviews.
summary.outcome: PR #584 was successfully shipped and merged to main with all CI checks green. The pipeline surfaced and fixed a security bug (T-66-E1 write authority escalation), restored deleted spec coverage (863 tests), fixed several real bugs found by reviewers, and resolved all 26 CodeRabbit findings (19 inline threads + 7 body comments).

repo: The mock-ipns-routing server entry compiles to dist/index.js, but ci.yml's SDK E2E job had node dist/server.js since PR #318 — it silently crashed (& masks the exit code) so the server never ran in CI; only Test 15 (the seqFloor network-resolve path) depended on it and thus failed

THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET is set only on the test step in the CI workflow, not the API process — so the header-bypass path silently fails in CI and all localhost traffic shares one per-IP throttle bucket, causing 429s under heavy suite load

CodeRabbit review comments are split across three distinct locations: resolvable inline threads, body-level 'Nitpick' sections, and body-level 'Outside diff range' sections — the latter two are not resolvable threads and require separate handling
jest coverageThreshold subtracts path-specific files (per-path entries) from the global computation — the 'All files' summary row can show below the global threshold while jest exits 0

Phase 66 deleted all shares spec files without rewriting them, leaving jest per-file coverage thresholds at 0% for those paths — CI failed on the first run with no failing tests, only threshold violations
The GSD commit helper consistently times out via 1Password signing and reports commit_failed (exit 143), but the commit actually lands — always verify with git log, never retry blindly
api:generate's trailing repo-wide eslint step fails on gitignored Astro-generated files (landing/.astro/*) — this is a false failure; the actual client regeneration always succeeds regardless
zsh reserves 'status' as a built-in variable — polling scripts that assign to a variable named 'status' fail silently with unexpected behavior

The fire-and-forget delegated-routing publish is an unreliable test dependency: it's a detached promise with retries, and under CI load it can be dropped before the test's resolve call — tests that depend on it should use unit mocks instead

Internal DB-state manipulation in sdk-e2e tests (direct psql to set signed_record=NULL/garbage) is a code smell — such states are unreachable through the API, the behavior belongs in unit tests with mocks

code.finding: SDK E2E job started mock routing with 'node dist/server.js &' — the phantom filename silently crashed on startup; correct entry is 'node dist/index.js'. Also replaced the blind 'sleep 2' with a /health poll so a dead server fails the job loudly instead of masking the crash.

Added 'if (process.env.NODE_ENV === 'test') { return true; }' at the top of canActivate to disable all rate limiting in the test environment — the only correct fix for the CI SDK-E2E throttle starvation issue.

T-66-E1: the claim path set writeDescriptorRef from dto.writeDescriptorRef without checking invite.writeDescriptorRef — a read-only invite with an attacker-supplied DTO could mint a write grant. Fix: gate on 'invite.writeDescriptorRef !== null' first.

SeqFloor gate: when signed_record IS NULL (shared-folder rows), the resolve endpoint must fail closed if the network record's sequence < floor — network records with lower seq than the DB floor must never be served ungated.

syncIpnsRecordSequence's update criteria had no sequence_number <= newSequenceNumber predicate — a stale TEE batch result could overwrite a row whose sequence was already advanced by a user publish. Added LessThanOrEqual(newSequenceNumber) to the criteria.

The delegated-routing publish is a detached/fire-and-forget promise — there is no await, no error surfacing to the caller. Under CI load with rate-limiting retries, the PUT can be dropped entirely before a test's resolve call.

PostToolUse hooks gsd-context-monitor.js and SessionStart gsd-check-update.js used relative paths (.claude/hooks/...) while all other GSD hooks use $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/hooks/... — whenever a Bash command cd'd into a subdir, node resolved the relative path from that subdir and threw cjs/loader:1433.

workflow: For parallel spec-authoring tasks (multiple independent files with no write conflicts), fan out via Workflow with one agent per file — synthesize with a central full coverage run rather than trusting per-agent scoped coverage numbers

The correct triage rule for pre-existing design decisions (e.g. same-seq CID idempotent-republish per D-09) is defer-with-todo even when CodeRabbit flags them as Critical — the existing unit test asserting the behavior is the authoritative signal

When a test requires setting internal DB state unreachable through the API (e.g. signed_record=NULL), move it to unit tests with mocks — the e2e version creates fragile dependencies on implementation details and CI-environment timing
Always verify subagent code changes adversarially: run the specs yourself and check that the assertions are genuine (not just passing on the fixed code, but also failing on the pre-fix code)
The greptile 'outside of diff range' comments land as issue-body comments, not resolvable review threads — they require manual inspection via the GitHub URL the user provides

friction: The mock-routing CI failure had two red herrings investigated before the real cause: first the throttle hypothesis (wrong), then the propagation-delay/poll approach (user rejected as bypassing the real publish), before discovering the phantom dist/server.js entry that had been broken since PR #318

CodeRabbit review findings are split across three distinct surfaces (inline threads, review body nitpicks, outside-diff body sections) with no single query that surfaces all of them — required multiple separate fetch strategies

The GSD commit helper times out consistently due to 1Password signing latency, reporting commit_failed (exit 143) while the commit actually lands — every commit required a follow-up git log verification step

zsh reserves 'status' as a built-in, silently breaking a background CI poll script that assigned to a variable named 'status' — required discovering via exit code 1 and rewriting with a different variable name

The release bot pushes a chore(release) commit to the branch after gh pr create AND after each passing Release Preview — required fetch+rebase before every push, easy to forget and results in a rejected push

api:generate's repo-wide trailing eslint step fails on gitignored Astro-generated files, making it appear the client regeneration failed when the actual output is correct — misleading signal requiring semantic diffing to confirm
open_items: ipns-records-root-uniqueness-index: add partial unique index on (userId) WHERE is_root to enforce one root record per user at DB level
ipns-first-publish-insert-race: first-publish INSERT can race under concurrent requests — needs an INSERT ... ON CONFLICT or advisory lock
ipns-idempotent-same-seq-cid-equivocation: the D-09 TEE re-sign behavior (allow different CID at same seq) conflicts with CodeRabbit's idempotency suggestion — needs a formal design decision
share-invite-validate-root-ownership: no check that the sharer actually owns the rootIpnsName they embed in an invite — heavy-lift design question
share-invite-reclaim-apply-later-grant: idempotent re-claim returns the existing share without applying a later invite's upgraded grant — fails safe today but under-specified
share-invites-claim-count-check-constraint: no DB-level CHECK ensuring claim_count stays in expected bounds
restore-shares-module-unit-coverage: share-invite.service lifecycle (create/list/revoke with full edge cases) still lacks deep unit coverage beyond the claim path
shares-bulk-revoke-direct-delete: revokeForItems loads full bytea Share rows into memory before deletion — safe to replace with manager.delete() but requires mock rewrite
phase68-web-share-stubs-gate-ui: web ShareDialog and share/invite services throw deferred stubs that surface as fake empty-state (no error flag) — needs UI gating in Phase 68
66-LEARNINGS.md and STATE.md Last Activity update are uncommitted local changes on main — need a branch and PR to land them
